sources.title: Effect of High-Intensity Strength Training on Knee Pain and Knee Joint Compressive Forces Among Adults With Knee Osteoarthritis: The START Randomized Clinical Trial

access.details: PMC full HTML inspected including Methods, Tables and harms. Supplement not retrieved.

integrity.method: Source record and Europe PMC REST core metadata inspected, including commentCorrectionList and firstPublicationDate; selected DOI correction/retraction web searches; no formal registry-wide audit.
integrity.result: Indexed related records: Comment in 34100874. These are comments/reprint links, not identified corrections/retractions; bounded check only.

sources.population: Ambulatory adults >=50; BMI 20–45; medial tibiofemoral KL 2–3 OA. Severe patellofemoral/lateral-predominant OA excluded; nonsurgical exercise study.
sources.comparator: High-intensity vs low-intensity strength vs attention workshops.
sources.coInterventions: Usual medication continued; ten-exercise upper/lower/core program and behavioral support.
sources.outcomes: 18-month WOMAC pain high vs control MD 0.2/20 (95%CI−0.6, 1.1); high vs low 0.7 (−0.1, 1.6). Walking compressive-force high vs control−58 N (−282, 165). No primary superiority.
sources.uncertainty: Single center; missing biomechanical data; no inference that all strengthening is ineffective/harmful.
sources.harms: Nonserious events 53/30/4; serious 5/3/5 unrelated to study (high/low/control).
sources.limitations: Single center; missing biomechanical data; no inference that all strengthening is ineffective/harmful.

protocol.execution: Six unilateral lower-body machine exercises including knee extension/press, plus four upper/core exercises.
protocol.dose: High: 3 sets, 75%1RM 8 reps weeks 1–2; 80%8 weeks 3–4; 85%6 weeks 5–6; 90%4 weeks 7–8. Low: 3x 15, 30–40%1RM.
protocol.frequency: Three supervised sessions/week, 18 months; 5 min warmup, 40 min training, 15 min cooldown.
protocol.supervision: Staff interventionists; four technique sessions precede 1RM testing.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as a universal numeric pain-stop criterion

sources.design: Systematic review/network meta-analysis; 217 RCTs, 15684 participants; search through August 2024.
sources.population: Knee OA; varied exercise modalities and protocols, predominantly conservative treatment.
sources.comparator: Aerobic, strengthening, flexibility, mind-body, neuromotor, mixed exercise and controls.
sources.coInterventions: Heterogeneous across trials; component effects not assured.
sources.outcomes: Moderate certainty: aerobic pain SMD−1.10 (95%CI−1.68,−0.52) at 4 weeks and−1.19 (−1.59,−0.79) at 12 weeks; strengthening function SMD 0.86 (0.53, 1.18) at 12 weeks. Rankings do not determine individual superiority or dosing.
sources.uncertainty: Network indirectness, heterogeneity, sparse harm reporting; published 2025 synthesis does not establish a specific safe app routine.
sources.harms: Safety reported in 40 studies(18%); no clear differences, wide uncertainty.
sources.limitations: Network indirectness, heterogeneity, sparse harm reporting; published 2025 synthesis does not establish a specific safe app routine.

proposedRules.statement: Retain unilateral machine strengthening as a clinical-content review candidate within individualized OA exercise care. Do not automatically import START intensity blocks or catalog progression.

applicability.stage: Stable symptomatic conservative care; flare severity not standardized.

proposedRules.limitations: Candidate only; machine variant and ordinary-workout symptom handling still need review.

gaps: Researcher appraisal, not formal GRADE: moderate confidence in individualized exercise strategy; low confidence in one exact ordinary-workout dose or contraindication.
No universal knee-flexion ceiling, maximum load or pain cutoff established.
START machine setup/range and independent component effects not established; 1RM calibration was supervised.

Independent clinical review absent; doses are reported study protocols, not app prescriptions.
